The current conditions in Abuja are characterized by a warm temperature of 25°C, which feels more like 31°C due to the high humidity of 90%. This is not unusual for this time of year, as the city is known for its hot and humid climate during the dry season. The wind is almost nonexistent, with a speed of just 2 km/h, making it feel even more oppressive. If you're planning on spending time outdoors, be sure to stay hydrated and take breaks in the shade, especially if you're walking around the National Assembly Complex or exploring the Wuse Market.

As we look ahead to the coming days, we can expect the heat to continue, with daytime temperatures soaring into the mid-to-upper 30s. This will make for some uncomfortable conditions, especially during the peak sun hours when the UV index is at its highest. However, it's worth noting that the nights will remain relatively mild, with temperatures dipping into the mid-20s. This could provide some relief for those who prefer cooler evenings, and it's a good idea to take advantage of this time to get outside and enjoy the city, perhaps with a stroll along the Jabi Lake or a visit to the Abuja National Mosque.

One thing to keep in mind is that the traffic on major roads like the Nnamdi Azikiwe Expressway could become more congested as the week progresses, especially if we do see some rain. While the current traffic is light, with speeds of 38 km/h, which is equivalent to the free-flow speed, this could change quickly if the roads become wet. It's always a good idea to check the latest traffic conditions before heading out, especially if you're planning on commuting to or from the city center.
